hyp_207e7a763b19.title: Router balance sweeping allows liquidity withdrawers to steal unrelated assets
hyp_207e7a763b19.description:
VULNERABILITY TYPE: security_issue
ROOT CAUSE: Output amounts are derived from balanceOf(address(this)) after external calls without recording pre-operation balances and calculating only the delta attributable to the current call.
ATTACK VECTOR: Send or wait for BASE/WBNB to accumulate in Router, acquire or use a valid LP position, then invoke the BNB liquidity withdrawal or single-sided withdrawal path; alternatively invoke swapAssetToSynth and receive synths backed by the Router's entire BASE balance.
AFFECTED NODES: router, user_router_entry, pool
AFFECTED CODE: contracts/Router.sol:removeLiquidityExact, contracts/Router.sol:removeLiquiditySingle, contracts/Router.sol:swapAssetToSynth
SEVERITY: high
REASONING: The code explicitly reads the Router's full BASE/WBNB balance after Pool.remove or sellTo and transfers the full balance, rather than measuring the balance before the operation. The same full-balance behavior is used when forwarding BASE before mintSynth.
SUGGESTED MITIGATION: Record each relevant Router asset balance before the operation and transfer only the post-operation balance delta. Avoid retaining user funds in Router; add explicit sweeping controls for any pre-existing balances and validate all intermediate transfer amounts.
hyp_207e7a763b19.reasoning: The code explicitly reads the Router's full BASE/WBNB balance after Pool.remove or sellTo and transfers the full balance, rather than measuring the balance before the operation. The same full-balance behavior is used when forwarding BASE before mintSynth.
hyp_207e7a763b19.mitigation: Record each relevant Router asset balance before the operation and transfer only the post-operation balance delta. Avoid retaining user funds in Router; add explicit sweeping controls for any pre-existing balances and validate all intermediate transfer amounts.
hyp_207e7a763b19.finding_description: Several Router paths transfer the entire current Router balance instead of only the assets produced by the current operation. In removeLiquidityExact for BNB, removeLiquiditySingle, and swapAssetToSynth, pre-existing BASE/WBNB balances can be included in the caller's output or used to mint synths. Any user able to execute the relevant path, such as an LP holder, can exploit assets accidentally sent to the Router, residual dust, or balances left by another operation.
hyp_207e7a763b19.impact: Attackers can appropriate unrelated BASE/WBNB held by Router or mint synths against those funds, causing direct loss of protocol or user assets.
hyp_207e7a763b19.qa_comment: Upon reviewing Router.removeLiquidityExact, Router.removeLiquiditySingle, and Router.swapAssetToSynth, I confirmed an exploitable balance-sweeping vulnerability. In removeLiquidityExact for the BNB pool, Pool.remove() sends BASE and WBNB to the Router, after which the Router reads its entire BASE and WBNB balances and transfers or unwraps them, without recording balances before the operation. More significantly, removeLiquiditySingle always calls Pool.remove() to send both assets to the Router; when toBase is true, it transfers only the token balance back to the pool, leaving the removed BASE stranded in the Router. A subsequent user with any valid LP position can invoke the opposite withdrawal path, which transfers the Router’s entire BASE balance into the pool and ultimately sends the resulting asset to that user. The same issue exists in swapAssetToSynth, where the Router forwards its complete BASE balance after sellTo, allowing pre-existing BASE to fund another user’s synth mint. No access control or balance-delta accounting prevents these transfers.

hyp_f0bf4a114496.title: Curated-pool dividend payouts are unlimited despite maxTrades configuration
hyp_f0bf4a114496.description:
VULNERABILITY TYPE: economic_attack
ROOT CAUSE: maxTrades is used only as a divisor in the payout calculation; there is no enforced per-era trade/dividend count or aggregate allocation cap before calling Reserve.grantFunds.
ATTACK VECTOR: Use repeated swaps against a curated pool, potentially with controlled fee sizes and LP ownership, to invoke getsDividend/addDividend many more than maxTrades times during the same era.
AFFECTED NODES: router, reserve, pool, user_router_entry
AFFECTED CODE: contracts/Router.sol:getsDividend, contracts/Router.sol:addDividend, contracts/Router.sol:addTradeFee
SEVERITY: high
REASONING: The payout formula uses reserve / eraLength / maxTrades, but the supplied implementation performs a Reserve grant on every qualifying swap and contains no visible counter, era boundary check, or cumulative cap. Repeated calls therefore multiply the nominal per-trade allocation.
SUGGESTED MITIGATION: Track dividend events and cumulative dividend allocation per era, reset the counters at an explicit era boundary, and reject or cap payouts once maxTrades or the configured aggregate allocation is reached. Enforce the cap in the Reserve as a defense in depth.
hyp_f0bf4a114496.reasoning: The payout formula uses reserve / eraLength / maxTrades, but the supplied implementation performs a Reserve grant on every qualifying swap and contains no visible counter, era boundary check, or cumulative cap. Repeated calls therefore multiply the nominal per-trade allocation.
hyp_f0bf4a114496.mitigation: Track dividend events and cumulative dividend allocation per era, reset the counters at an explicit era boundary, and reject or cap payouts once maxTrades or the configured aggregate allocation is reached. Enforce the cap in the Reserve as a defense in depth.
hyp_f0bf4a114496.finding_description: addDividend computes dailyAllocation using maxTrades but does not track or enforce the maximum number of dividend events per era, and the shown Router state includes no effective per-era payout counter or reset in this path. A caller can repeatedly trade against a curated pool while emissions are enabled and trigger repeated Reserve grants, allowing the reserve allocation intended for a bounded number of trades to be paid out repeatedly.
hyp_f0bf4a114496.impact: The Reserve can be drained faster than intended, transferring protocol incentives to the curated pool and its LP holders and reducing funds available for other protocol obligations.
hyp_f0bf4a114496.qa_comment: Upon reviewing Router.sol functions getsDividend, addTradeFee, and addDividend, I confirmed that the configured maxTrades value is not enforced as a per-era event limit or cumulative allocation cap. For every qualifying curated-pool swap, getsDividend calls addTradeFee and then addDividend, while addDividend calculates dailyAllocation as the current Reserve balance divided by eraLength and maxTrades, and immediately calls Reserve.grantFunds. No trade counter, era identifier, reset mechanism, or aggregate dividend tracking exists. Consequently, after the fee-average window is populated and emissions are enabled, an attacker can repeatedly execute swaps against a curated pool and trigger additional grants beyond maxTrades events in the same era. Reserve.grantFunds only limits each transfer to the reserve's current balance and does not impose a Router-specific budget; although the reserve balance declines, repeated calls can cumulatively distribute substantially more than the intended era allocation and can continue until the reserve is depleted. The curated-pool and nonzero-average checks are eligibility conditions, not rate limits.

hyp_e8487d8d134a.title: Router ignores token transfer return values and received amounts in asset ingress and egress
hyp_e8487d8d134a.description:
VULNERABILITY TYPE: security_issue
ROOT CAUSE: Unsafe ERC20/BEP20 interaction patterns and failure to require successful transfers or consistently use balance-delta amounts for downstream accounting.
ATTACK VECTOR: Use a listed 18-decimal token with non-standard or fee-on-transfer behavior, or interact during a token transfer failure, causing Router to proceed after a failed/short transfer; the resulting operation can strand funds, mint incorrect LP amounts, or silently fail user payouts.
AFFECTED NODES: router, user_router_entry, pool_factory
AFFECTED CODE: contracts/Router.sol:_handleTransferIn, contracts/Router.sol:_handleTransferOut, contracts/Router.sol:addLiquidityForMember, contracts/Router.sol:buyTo, contracts/Router.sol:sellTo
SEVERITY: medium
REASONING: The code invokes transferFrom, transfer, and WBNB transfer without checking their boolean results. Although _handleTransferIn calculates a balance delta for ERC20 inputs, callers ignore the returned actual value and continue using requested amounts in their control flow.
SUGGESTED MITIGATION: Use SafeERC20-style wrappers that revert on false or malformed return data, measure pre/post balances for every input, and pass the actual received amount into Pool operations. Verify output transfer success before finalizing accounting.
hyp_e8487d8d134a.reasoning: The code invokes transferFrom, transfer, and WBNB transfer without checking their boolean results. Although _handleTransferIn calculates a balance delta for ERC20 inputs, callers ignore the returned actual value and continue using requested amounts in their control flow.
hyp_e8487d8d134a.mitigation: Use SafeERC20-style wrappers that revert on false or malformed return data, measure pre/post balances for every input, and pass the actual received amount into Pool operations. Verify output transfer success before finalizing accounting.
hyp_e8487d8d134a.finding_description: _handleTransferIn calls transferFrom or WBNB transfer without checking the returned boolean, and its computed actual amount is not used by the public liquidity and swap entrypoints. _handleTransferOut likewise ignores the return value of ERC20 transfer. For tokens that return false or otherwise do not transfer the requested amount, Router can continue into Pool accounting as though the operation succeeded, while users may receive no output or LP/swap accounting may become inconsistent.
hyp_e8487d8d134a.impact: Users can lose input assets without receiving the expected LP tokens or swap output, and pools can become misaccounted or unusable for affected assets.
hyp_e8487d8d134a.qa_comment: Upon reviewing the Router transfer paths and PoolFactory.createPoolADD, I confirmed an exploitable unsafe-token interaction vulnerability. Router._handleTransferIn computes a balance delta for ERC20 inputs but does not require transferFrom to return true, and addLiquidityForMember, buyTo, sellTo, and related callers ignore the returned actual amount and continue using the requested amount in subsequent Pool operations. Router._handleTransferOut similarly invokes ERC20 transfer without checking its return value; therefore, a token that returns false can cause a swap or liquidity-removal operation to complete while the user receives no payout, leaving assets stranded in the Router. The WBNB transfer in _handleTransferIn is also unchecked. PoolFactory._handleTransferIn has the same unchecked transferFrom pattern during createPoolADD. Although some failed transfers may cause downstream Pool logic to revert depending on its balance checks, no general guard prevents silent false-return transfers or fee-on-transfer discrepancies, and balance-delta results are not propagated. A listed or newly created token with non-standard or fee-on-transfer behavior can therefore produce incorrect accounting or silent payout failures.

hyp_4f27d10bb008.title: BondVault claim logic can permanently lock half of a member’s remaining LP
hyp_4f27d10bb008.description:
VULNERABILITY TYPE: logic_error
ROOT CAUSE: The final-claim test compares the claim amount with bondedLP after subtraction instead of comparing it with the pre-claim balance or checking whether the remaining balance is zero.
ATTACK VECTOR: A DAO-triggered claim, including a claim initiated during a subsequent vault operation, can occur around the halfway point of a vesting period; the affected member then has a positive balance with a zero claim rate.
AFFECTED NODES: bond_vault, dao
AFFECTED CODE: contracts/BondVault.sol:claimForMember, contracts/BondVault.sol:calcBondedLP
SEVERITY: high
REASONING: The state update visibly occurs before the equality test: bondedLP is decremented and then _claimable is compared to the new bondedLP. At a 50% claim, the remaining balance equals the claim amount, so claimRate is zeroed while bondedLP remains positive.
SUGGESTED MITIGATION: Capture the pre-claim bonded balance, determine whether _claimable equals that pre-claim balance, and set claimRate to zero only when the post-claim bondedLP is zero. Add tests for claims at zero, half, and full vesting.
hyp_4f27d10bb008.reasoning: The state update visibly occurs before the equality test: bondedLP is decremented and then _claimable is compared to the new bondedLP. At a 50% claim, the remaining balance equals the claim amount, so claimRate is zeroed while bondedLP remains positive.
hyp_4f27d10bb008.mitigation: Capture the pre-claim bonded balance, determine whether _claimable equals that pre-claim balance, and set claimRate to zero only when the post-claim bondedLP is zero. Add tests for claims at zero, half, and full vesting.
hyp_4f27d10bb008.finding_description: claimForMember subtracts _claimable from bondedLP and then checks whether _claimable equals the post-claim bondedLP. When a claim occurs at exactly half of the remaining vesting amount, the comparison succeeds even though LP remains, causing claimRate to be set to zero. The remaining LP can no longer vest unless another deposit resets the rate or DAO release is invoked.
hyp_4f27d10bb008.impact: Members can have part of their bonded LP permanently locked, resulting in loss or indefinite denial of access to redeemable liquidity.
hyp_4f27d10bb008.qa_comment: Upon reviewing BondVault.sol, I confirmed the logic error in claimForMember and calcBondedLP. calcBondedLP computes the unlocked amount using elapsed time and claimRate, and claimForMember then updates lastBlockTime and subtracts _claimable from bondedLP before executing the final-claim test. The condition at the relevant code in claimForMember, `if (_claimable == mapBondAsset_memberDetails[asset].bondedLP[member])`, compares the claim against the post-claim remainder rather than the pre-claim balance or zero. Consequently, when exactly half of a bond is claimable, the subtraction leaves the other half in bondedLP, making the equality true and setting claimRate to zero. Subsequent calls to calcBondedLP therefore return zero despite the positive bondedLP balance, so the remaining LP cannot vest or be claimed through normal claim functions. The path is reachable because Dao.claimForMember and claimAllForMember invoke the vault, and depositForMember can also trigger claimForMember. No guard corrects the rate afterward; only a new deposit or release can potentially change the state.

hyp_bb979dd4a209.title: Integer truncation can create permanently unclaimable BondVault dust
hyp_bb979dd4a209.description:
VULNERABILITY TYPE: funds_lockup
ROOT CAUSE: The vesting rate is rounded down to whole LP units per second without preserving fractional accrual or a remainder accumulator.
ATTACK VECTOR: A member can be assigned a small bond or be left with a small residual balance after vesting claims; the resulting claimRate becomes zero and the residual cannot be claimed through normal vesting.
AFFECTED NODES: bond_vault, dao
AFFECTED CODE: contracts/BondVault.sol:depositForMember, contracts/BondVault.sol:calcBondedLP, contracts/BondVault.sol:claimForMember
SEVERITY: medium
REASONING: The rate assignment uses bondedLP / bondingPeriodSeconds with Solidity integer truncation, and claimability is calculated solely as elapsed time multiplied by that rate. No fractional remainder or minimum-rate handling exists.
SUGGESTED MITIGATION: Track vesting using a numerator and denominator or an accrued remainder so fractional per-second entitlement is preserved. Alternatively provide a clearly defined final-dust claim path that does not depend on bondRelease.
hyp_bb979dd4a209.reasoning: The rate assignment uses bondedLP / bondingPeriodSeconds with Solidity integer truncation, and claimability is calculated solely as elapsed time multiplied by that rate. No fractional remainder or minimum-rate handling exists.
hyp_bb979dd4a209.mitigation: Track vesting using a numerator and denominator or an accrued remainder so fractional per-second entitlement is preserved. Alternatively provide a clearly defined final-dust claim path that does not depend on bondRelease.
hyp_bb979dd4a209.finding_description: depositForMember computes claimRate using integer division of bondedLP by bondingPeriodSeconds. Any deposit smaller than the vesting period, and any residual amount below that period after claims, receives a zero claim rate. calcBondedLP then returns zero indefinitely because elapsed time multiplied by the zero rate is zero.
hyp_bb979dd4a209.impact: Bonded LP amounts can remain trapped in BondVault indefinitely, requiring administrative release or another deposit to recover them.
hyp_bb979dd4a209.qa_comment: Upon reviewing BondVault.depositForMember, calcBondedLP, and claimForMember in contracts/BondVault.sol, I confirmed the funds-lockup condition. depositForMember calculates claimRate as bondedLP divided by bondingPeriodSeconds using integer division, with no remainder accounting. Consequently, any deposit whose LP amount is smaller than the configured vesting period (15,552,000 seconds by default) receives a zero claimRate. calcBondedLP then computes elapsed time multiplied by this zero rate and returns zero unless the privileged bondRelease flag is enabled, so the member cannot obtain the bonded LPs through Dao.claimForMember or claimAllForMember. The same issue can affect residual amounts only where a recalculation produces a zero rate; ordinary nonzero-rate residuals eventually become claimable because calcBondedLP caps claims at the remaining balance. The only apparent escape is BondVault.release(), restricted to the DAO or deployer and not exposed through a normal user path. Thus, the vulnerable zero-rate case is exploitable as a user funds lockup, although an authorized administrative release may recover all bonds globally.

hyp_162dcf373df3.title: BondVault ignores LP transfer failure during claims
hyp_162dcf373df3.description:
VULNERABILITY TYPE: unchecked_external_call
ROOT CAUSE: The return value of the BEP20 transfer is discarded after claim state is irreversibly updated.
ATTACK VECTOR: If the resolved pool token is non-compliant, paused, or otherwise returns false on transfer, a member claim can execute successfully from the vault’s perspective without transferring LP.
AFFECTED NODES: bond_vault, pool_factory, pool
AFFECTED CODE: contracts/BondVault.sol:claimForMember
SEVERITY: medium
REASONING: The code explicitly ignores the bool result from iBEP20.transfer. State is reduced before the call, so a false return cannot be safely retried without separate recovery logic.
SUGGESTED MITIGATION: Require the transfer result to be true, or use a safe-transfer wrapper that reverts when the token returns false or malformed data. Consider performing the transfer before finalizing accounting only where reentrancy protections preserve consistency.
hyp_162dcf373df3.reasoning: The code explicitly ignores the bool result from iBEP20.transfer. State is reduced before the call, so a false return cannot be safely retried without separate recovery logic.
hyp_162dcf373df3.mitigation: Require the transfer result to be true, or use a safe-transfer wrapper that reverts when the token returns false or malformed data. Consider performing the transfer before finalizing accounting only where reentrancy protections preserve consistency.
hyp_162dcf373df3.finding_description: claimForMember decreases the member’s bondedLP and recalculates weights before calling iBEP20(_pool).transfer(member, _claimable), but it does not check the returned boolean. A pool token that returns false without reverting causes the vault to record the claim as completed even though no LP was delivered.
hyp_162dcf373df3.impact: Claimed LP can be permanently lost from the member’s accounting and remain in the vault or pool-token contract, producing an unrecoverable shortfall.
hyp_162dcf373df3.qa_comment: Upon reviewing the alleged unchecked external call in BondVault.claimForMember, I determined this is a false positive for the deployed architecture. The function does discard the boolean returned by iBEP20(_pool).transfer(member, _claimable) after updating accounting and invoking decreaseWeight, but _pool is obtained from PoolFactory.getPool(asset), whose mappings are populated only with contracts deployed directly via new Pool(...). Pool.transfer() unconditionally calls _transfer() and returns true on success; it does not contain a false-return path. If the vault lacks sufficient LP balance, _transfer() reverts, and Solidity transaction atomicity rolls back the prior timestamp, bondedLP, claim-rate, and weight updates. The underlying asset token’s transfer behavior is irrelevant because claims transfer the Pool’s LP token, not the underlying token. Although checking the return value would be defensive best practice, the supplied code does not provide a practical route for a non-compliant token or false return from the resolved pool. A different factory implementation or upgradeable pool design could change this conclusion, but neither is shown here.

hyp_500b2cb11180.title: Harvested Synth rewards bypass the minimum withdrawal lock
hyp_500b2cb11180.description:
VULNERABILITY TYPE: logic_error
ROOT CAUSE: The withdrawal lock is tracked only when deposits are made, while harvestSingle increases the withdrawable balance without refreshing the lock timestamp.
ATTACK VECTOR: A member deposits synths, waits for the existing lock to expire, harvests rewards, and immediately calls withdraw to remove the newly credited rewards.
AFFECTED NODES: synth_vault, user_synth_entry
AFFECTED CODE: SynthVault.harvestSingle: credits mapMemberSynth_deposit without updating mapMember_depositTime, SynthVault._processWithdraw: checks only mapMember_depositTime
SEVERITY: medium
REASONING: The code explicitly updates mapMemberSynth_lastTime during harvest but does not update mapMember_depositTime, whereas withdrawal enforces only the latter timestamp. The harvested amount is therefore immediately included in the withdrawable balance after an earlier deposit lock has expired.
SUGGESTED MITIGATION: Apply the intended lock to harvested rewards by updating the applicable member or member-and-synth withdrawal timestamp when harvestSingle credits synthReward, or track deposit timestamps per balance tranche and enforce the lock against each tranche.
hyp_500b2cb11180.reasoning: The code explicitly updates mapMemberSynth_lastTime during harvest but does not update mapMember_depositTime, whereas withdrawal enforces only the latter timestamp. The harvested amount is therefore immediately included in the withdrawable balance after an earlier deposit lock has expired.
hyp_500b2cb11180.mitigation: Apply the intended lock to harvested rewards by updating the applicable member or member-and-synth withdrawal timestamp when harvestSingle credits synthReward, or track deposit timestamps per balance tranche and enforce the lock against each tranche.
hyp_500b2cb11180.finding_description: harvestSingle credits newly minted synths to mapMemberSynth_deposit but never updates mapMember_depositTime. Since withdraw checks only the older global deposit timestamp, a member can harvest newly accrued rewards and immediately withdraw them without waiting minimumDepositTime.
hyp_500b2cb11180.impact: Users can immediately exit with freshly harvested rewards, defeating the intended one-hour lock and enabling short-term or mercenary participation that the lock was intended to prevent.
hyp_500b2cb11180.qa_comment: Upon reviewing the SynthVault deposit, harvestSingle, calcCurrentReward, and _processWithdraw functions, I confirmed that the alleged lock-bypass vulnerability is exploitable. _deposit updates both mapMemberSynth_lastTime and the member-wide mapMember_depositTime to block.timestamp + minimumDepositTime. However, harvestSingle only refreshes mapMemberSynth_lastTime before adding synthReward to mapMemberSynth_deposit; it does not update mapMember_depositTime. Once the original deposit lock expires, a member can call harvestSingle, which is permitted because calcCurrentReward checks only the synth-specific timestamp, and the newly minted reward is immediately added to the withdrawable balance. The member can then call withdraw, whose _processWithdraw function checks only block.timestamp > mapMember_depositTime[_member], allowing withdrawal of a percentage of the combined principal and harvested rewards without a new lock period. No later check uses the refreshed synth-specific timestamp to restrict withdrawal, and harvestAll has the same underlying behavior because it delegates to harvestSingle. Therefore, the implementation does not enforce the intended withdrawal lock on harvested rewards.

hyp_063f529d178e.title: SynthVault harvestAll becomes increasingly gas-heavy and can become unusable
hyp_063f529d178e.description:
VULNERABILITY TYPE: denial_of_service
ROOT CAUSE: An unbounded historical asset array is used as the loop domain for a user-facing state-changing function, with no pagination or bounded iteration.
ATTACK VECTOR: As the number of valid synth assets grows, a user calls harvestAll and eventually exceeds the block gas limit, preventing the user from harvesting through this function and potentially making the standard harvest path unusable for affected users.
AFFECTED NODES: synth_vault, user_synth_entry, synth_registry
AFFECTED CODE: SynthVault.harvestAll: loops from index 0 through stakedSynthAssets.length, SynthVault._deposit: permanently appends each first-seen synth to stakedSynthAssets
SEVERITY: medium
REASONING: The loop bound is historical and monotonically increasing, and each iteration can make multiple external calls. The exact exploitability depends on how many synths can be curated and staked, but the implementation has no scalability bound or pagination mechanism.
SUGGESTED MITIGATION: Provide paginated harvesting with start and end indexes, or let users harvest only explicitly selected synths. Do not require iterating over the full historical stakedSynthAssets array in one transaction.
hyp_063f529d178e.reasoning: The loop bound is historical and monotonically increasing, and each iteration can make multiple external calls. The exact exploitability depends on how many synths can be curated and staked, but the implementation has no scalability bound or pagination mechanism.
hyp_063f529d178e.mitigation: Provide paginated harvesting with start and end indexes, or let users harvest only explicitly selected synths. Do not require iterating over the full historical stakedSynthAssets array in one transaction.
hyp_063f529d178e.finding_description: harvestAll iterates over the entire stakedSynthAssets array on every call. The array permanently grows whenever a new synth is first deposited and entries are never removed, while each eligible entry performs reward calculation and may invoke reserve and pool contracts.
hyp_063f529d178e.impact: HarvestAll can revert due to gas exhaustion, leaving users unable to claim rewards through the aggregate function and imposing increasingly high gas costs as historical synth assets accumulate.
hyp_063f529d178e.qa_comment: Upon reviewing SynthVault.harvestAll and _deposit, I confirmed the reported scalability-related denial-of-service condition. harvestAll iterates from index zero through the entire stakedSynthAssets array on every call, without pagination, a caller-supplied range, or any membership-based index. _deposit permanently appends each previously unseen synth to this array via isStakedSynth and push, so the loop domain is monotonically increasing and is never pruned. Although non-member entries generally avoid the more expensive harvestSingle path because their calculated reward is zero, every entry still incurs storage reads, timestamp checks, and reward calculation, while entries with an active balance and reward can trigger multiple external calls through the reserve, pool factory, pool, utilities, and synth contracts. A user can expand the global array by depositing across many valid synths, subject to synth and pool curation. No guard limits the array size or bounds gas usage. harvestSingle remains an alternative for individual assets, so this does not necessarily disable all harvesting, but harvestAll can eventually exceed the block gas limit and become unusable as historical assets accumulate.

hyp_f352a4505325.title: Withdrawal basis points are not range-validated, enabling caller-triggered reverts and inconsistent partial accounting
hyp_f352a4505325.description:
VULNERABILITY TYPE: validation_error
ROOT CAUSE: The external withdrawal parameter is not constrained to the documented basis-point range and deposit and weight reductions are independently rounded.
ATTACK VECTOR: A caller supplies basisPoints above 10000 to force withdrawal failure, or uses a small partial basis-point value against a dust-sized weight so principal decreases while weight remains unchanged, then harvests against the retained weight before final withdrawal.
AFFECTED NODES: synth_vault, user_synth_entry
AFFECTED CODE: SynthVault.withdraw: forwards unrestricted basisPoints, SynthVault._processWithdraw: independently calculates and subtracts principal and weight
SEVERITY: medium
REASONING: There is no explicit require that basisPoints <= 10000. The two calcPart operations can round differently because deposit and weight are separate quantities, allowing accounting divergence for small positions. The practical excess depends on Utils.calcPart precision and the asset-to-weight ratio.
SUGGESTED MITIGATION: Require basisPoints <= 10000 and reject zero or otherwise ineffective withdrawals where appropriate. Calculate a single proportional share and ensure principal and weight reductions cannot diverge materially due to rounding; clear residual weight when the corresponding deposit reaches zero.
hyp_f352a4505325.reasoning: There is no explicit require that basisPoints <= 10000. The two calcPart operations can round differently because deposit and weight are separate quantities, allowing accounting divergence for small positions. The practical excess depends on Utils.calcPart precision and the asset-to-weight ratio.
hyp_f352a4505325.mitigation: Require basisPoints <= 10000 and reject zero or otherwise ineffective withdrawals where appropriate. Calculate a single proportional share and ensure principal and weight reductions cannot diverge materially due to rounding; clear residual weight when the corresponding deposit reaches zero.
hyp_f352a4505325.finding_description: withdraw and _processWithdraw accept arbitrary basisPoints without requiring a value between 0 and 10000. Values above 10000 can produce a calculated amount greater than the recorded balance and cause subtraction underflow, while values that round one component to zero can remove deposit principal without proportionally removing its recorded weight.
hyp_f352a4505325.impact: Malformed requests can reliably revert, and rounding mismatches can let a member retain reward weight after reducing deposited synth principal, potentially receiving excess emissions relative to remaining capital.
hyp_f352a4505325.qa_comment: Upon reviewing SynthVault.withdraw and _processWithdraw, I confirmed that the stated validation and accounting weaknesses exist. withdraw forwards the caller-supplied basisPoints without enforcing a maximum of 10,000, while _processWithdraw independently invokes Utils.calcPart for the stored deposit and synth weight. With integer, floor-based proportional arithmetic, a partial withdrawal can therefore reduce mapMemberSynth_deposit while reducing mapMemberSynth_weight by zero when the weight is below the rounding threshold. The member can repeat such withdrawals and retain voting or reward weight after removing the corresponding synth principal, potentially harvesting rewards against stale weight before a later full withdrawal clears it. The global and per-member weight totals are updated using the independently rounded weight value, so no invariant repairs this divergence. A basisPoints value above 10,000 will generally cause subtraction underflow and revert under Solidity 0.8.3; this primarily makes the caller’s own transaction fail rather than harming other users, but it still demonstrates missing input validation. The lockout only restricts timing and does not prevent either issue.

hyp_ad3667485200.title: Arbitrary zero-value deposits can repeatedly lock another user’s SynthVault position
hyp_ad3667485200.description:
VULNERABILITY TYPE: denial_of_service
ROOT CAUSE: Public third-party deposits allow arbitrary member selection, and zero-value deposits still update lock state.
ATTACK VECTOR: Call depositForMember(validSynth, victim, 0) repeatedly. The zero transfer succeeds, then _deposit assigns future timestamps to the victim without adding assets.
AFFECTED NODES: synth_vault, user_synth_entry
AFFECTED CODE: SynthVault.depositForMember(address,address,uint256), SynthVault._deposit(address,address,uint256)
SEVERITY: high
REASONING: The function performs no positive-amount validation and does not restrict the member parameter. _deposit unconditionally writes mapMemberSynth_lastTime and mapMember_depositTime, so a zero-value call changes withdrawal and harvest eligibility despite adding no balance.
SUGGESTED MITIGATION: Add require(amount > 0), validate that the transferred amount is positive, and use an authorization model for deposits on behalf of another member or require explicit member consent.
hyp_ad3667485200.reasoning: The function performs no positive-amount validation and does not restrict the member parameter. _deposit unconditionally writes mapMemberSynth_lastTime and mapMember_depositTime, so a zero-value call changes withdrawal and harvest eligibility despite adding no balance.
hyp_ad3667485200.mitigation: Add require(amount > 0), validate that the transferred amount is positive, and use an authorization model for deposits on behalf of another member or require explicit member consent.
hyp_ad3667485200.finding_description: depositForMember is public, accepts any member address, and does not require amount > 0. A caller can invoke it with a valid synth, a victim address, and zero amount; transferFrom of zero succeeds, while _deposit still resets the victim’s global and per-synth lock timestamps.
hyp_ad3667485200.impact: An attacker can repeatedly reset a victim’s one-hour withdrawal and harvest lock at negligible cost, preventing the victim from withdrawing or harvesting their SynthVault position for as long as the attacker continues the calls.
hyp_ad3667485200.qa_comment: Upon reviewing the SynthVault deposit flow, I confirmed that the alleged denial-of-service vulnerability is exploitable. In depositForMember, the contract validates only that the synth is recognized and that transferFrom succeeds; it does not require amount to be greater than zero or restrict the member address. A caller can therefore invoke depositForMember(validSynth, victim, 0), subject to the token accepting a zero-value transferFrom. The subsequent _deposit call unconditionally sets mapMemberSynth_lastTime[_member][_synth] and mapMember_depositTime[_member] to block.timestamp + minimumDepositTime, even when _amount is zero. It also records the member as a synth member, although no deposit balance or weight is added. These timestamps directly gate calcCurrentReward/harvest eligibility and _processWithdraw, so repeated zero-value calls can continually extend the victim's withdrawal and harvest lockouts without adding assets. No authorization, consent, existing-membership, or positive-amount check mitigates this path. The impact depends on the synth token's zero-transfer behavior, but standard BEP-20 implementations generally permit zero transfers, making the attack path clear.
